title: Data that should never be on the device, and what the store makes you declare

videos.script:
The course ends with what should not be on the phone at all. {{key}} First, a secret. You build the planner with a service key in its configuration, then search the result, and find the key in one command. Anything in the app belongs to whoever downloads it. The fix is a server that holds the key.

{{tokens}} Second, the one secret a phone does keep: proof of who the person is. Two tokens, one that lives for minutes, one kept in the keystore and spent each time it is used. And a sign-out that wipes the device.

{{log}} Third, data nobody needed. A log line that carried a name and an address to a crash reporter.

{{stores}} And last, the forms both stores make you fill in, about everything you collect. They are easier to answer honestly when you keep less.
